result.title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
result.summary: Intermediate layers often outperform final layers when foundation models are used as frozen feature extractors, but the source of this advantage is unclear. We study this question in EEG foundation models by separating three factors: how representations are read out, whether intermediate layers provide predictive utility beyond the final-layer interface, and whether useful depth structure transfers across datasets. Across five models and three tasks, improving the final-layer readout consistently recovers substantial predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous within frozen extraction. We also find that layers selected on one dataset remain useful on another across five dataset pairs and four task families, and that a compact set of source-derived task directions retains predictive value after transfer in sleep staging. Together, these results show that predictive utility varies across depth, and its usefulness depends on how representations are read out and transferred. More crucially, source-selected layers provide a reusable feature interface across datasets, reducing the need for target-side layer search while outperforming final-layer baselines on target datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在五个 EEG 基础模型、三个任务上，将「读出方式」「中间层是否带来末层之外的预测增益」「深度结构能否跨数据集迁移」三因素分开考察，发现改进末层读出可大幅恢复性能，但冻结提取下中间层仍占优，且源数据集选出的层与任务方向可在目标数据集复用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「读出接口差异会左右表观深度优势」的结论，可供核查 LVR 中比较不同层 latent 信息量与可用性时如何区分读出方式与真实表征差异，以及源任务选层能否迁移为可复用的 latent 探针接口。
